title: Packet tests compile with native TypeScript 7
what: Pin typescript 7 in the test deps, and make kit_packet run the platform's native compiler binary directly (found the way getExePath.js finds it), with no JavaScript runtime; keep one clear refusal when the binary for this platform is missing. Check the tsc flags relay passes (-p, --noEmit false, --declaration) against 7.0's removed options, and measure the packet tests' time before and after.
why: 29 Oct, npm registry: typescript 7.0.2 is the latest stable (published 8 Jul 2026); the compiler is a native Go binary shipped per platform (@typescript/typescript-darwin-arm64 7.0.2, 27.5 MB unpacked; linux-x64 and linux-arm too), and the package's bin/tsc is only a 2-line JavaScript launcher (#!/usr/bin/env node, import ../lib/tsc.js, getExePath.js) that finds and starts that binary. relay pins typescript 6.0.3 (plugins/relay/tests/ts-deps/package.json), a JavaScript compiler, so the packet tests need node or bun to run it (the Linux-container fix runs `bun tsc` when node is missing). IP 70 chosen by the front.
pass_cases: the packet tests pass on the Mac and in the clean Linux container with neither node nor bun on PATH for the compile step
a platform with no native compiler package gets one line naming what to install
the packet tests' time before and after is written in the report
